feature: Camera label scan is a streaming auto-capture: the camera decodes frames continuously while the operator aims (ML Kit barcode every tick, OCR throttled to every 3rd) and captures one full-resolution frame by itself once the same decoded value stays stable across 2 consecutive ticks and the label box is large/centred enough — no tap or shutter. A hint appears after ~20s without a stable candidate; shutter and tap-rectangle manual capture remain as fallback. Applies to every camera scan entry point (receiving, CN scan, put-away, ad-hoc, shelf exchange, internal transfer, picking, print-product-label, measuring/verify).
reason: The tap/shutter → crop → OCR chain costs ~1.5-3s per scan and needs a steady hand; on a shelf full of labels operators want point-and-shoot decoding like a hardware scanner
remarks: Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-streaming-label-scan-design.md (amended same day: rule confirm + stream-frame result + analysis size). Branch feat/streaming-label-scan. Native: StreamingLabelGate (pure-Java rules gate — ALL of a named rule's keywords confirms; 21 unit tests) + StreamingLabelAnalyzer (persistent ML Kit clients, adaptive cadence, OCR on first tick) + RectangleCameraActivity stream mode (no full-res capture — firing analysis frame is the evidence photo, firing-tick barcodes ride along, matchedRule in result, torch off for label scan) + plugin scanLabel({stream, rules, analysisSize}). Web: captureLabel(options), [SCAN-TIME]/[SCAN-RESULT] logs, ad-hoc put-away wires KOA_LABEL_RULES + hd analysis. Measured T23X: open~1.2-1.5s (CameraX bind), fire~0.4-1s, fire→JS~0.1s. Server-side OCR decode API + native preview card parked for later design.
